title: Inquest calls for more help for alcohol abusers
article: The Yukon's coroner will lobby the government to find better ways of dealing with problem drinkers.
It's the top recommendation from the inquest into the death of Madeleine Henry.

The 41-year-old woman is the latest Yukoner to have died in police custody. She was taken to hospital after she stopped breathing while in the RCMP drunk tank and died in June 2000. Doctors testified at the inquest she had had toxic levels of alcohol in her system.
But the jury wants government and police to consider other ways of handling the city's chronic drinkers.
Coroner Sharon Hanley says she will do her best to make government agencies follow up.
"Well it's my position and mandate to put these forward. They're not under any obligation to carry them out, but we'll see what we can do," she says.
Whitehorse RCMP have already endorsed a program from Anchorage.
The Alaskan city has established a special program to look after problem drinkers.
